outcomeNote: A baraita correcting the mishna's account; no dialectic.

segments.he: מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁעָבְרוּ יוֹתֵר מֵאַרְבָּעִים זוּג וְעִיכְּבָן רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא כּוּ׳. תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: חַס וְשָׁלוֹם שֶׁרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא עִיכְּבָן. אֶלָּא שַׁזְפַּר רֹאשָׁהּ שֶׁל גֶּדֶר עִיכְּבָן, וְשִׁלַּח רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְהוֹרִידוּהוּ מִגְּדוּלָּתוֹ.
segments.en: § It was taught in the mishna: There was once «an incident where more than forty pairs» of witnesses «were passing» through on their way to Jerusalem to testify about the new moon, «and Rabbi Akiva detained them» in Lod, telling them that there was no need for them to desecrate Shabbat for this purpose. «It is taught» in a baraita: «Rabbi Yehuda said: Heaven forbid that Rabbi Akiva detained them,» for he would certainly not have made such an error. «Rather,» it was «that Zefer, the head of» the city of «Geder, detained them. And Rabban Gamliel sent and they removed him from his high» office because he had acted inappropriately.

positions.claim: Rabbi Akiva did not detain the witnesses; Zefer of Geder did, and Rabban Gamliel had him deposed
